principles: Keep market genre/category separate from mechanics, rules, goals, dynamics and player-value lenses.
Prefer external vocabularies and preserve source authority; Ordivon Next owns only the crosswalk and local evidence links.
A game may legitimately carry multiple genre/feature/activity labels even when a market-analysis taxonomy chooses one primary category.
Design search operates on mechanism graphs and couplings, not on selecting a genre first.
Mechanism composition predicts dynamics; Human play/evidence decides whether the intended experience actually occurs.
Do not treat this catalog as exhaustive. New externally grounded mechanisms extend it without forcing a global reclassification.
A normalized design element may belong to multiple mechanism families; family membership is faceted, not exclusive.

sources.name: Dormans — Simulating Mechanics to Study Emergence in Games

sources.name: GameRefinery genre / feature taxonomy

sources.name: Quantic Foundry Gamer Motivation Model
sources.use: player motivation lens; not a mechanism taxonomy

sources.name: Xbox Accessibility Guidelines
sources.use: cross-cutting accessibility and per-mechanic difficulty/input tuning

experienceLenses.law: Experience/motivation lenses are outcome hypotheses, not mechanics and not scalar product scores.

compositionModel.law: Genre is an output/market label over a composition; it is not the design primitive. Composition quality is empirical because dynamics can emerge unpredictably from coupled mechanics.
